title: WPMS/643/2009 of SMT SARITA DEVI Vs SADGURU YOGENDRA SHEEL NATH and OTHERS

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition No.643 of 2009 (M/S)
Smt Sarita Devi ....Petitioner
Versus
Shri Sadguru Yogendra Sheel Nath
(Dhuni Sansthan) and others
 ....Respondents
Mr Pankaj Miglani, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr Virendra Kaparwan, Advocate for the respondent nos.1 & 2.
Hon'ble V.K. Bist, J.

Present writ petition has been filed by the petitioner for
quashing the order dated 21.04.2009 passed by the
Additional District Judge/F.T.C.-Ist Dehradun in O.S. No.279
of 1984, Jaswant Singh vs Sadguru Yogendra. Further prayer
has also been made in the writ petition for allowing the
application paper no.165-A2 moved by the petitioner for
amendment in substitution application (Paper no.130-A)
moved on account of death of sole plaintiff (Jaswant Singh).
 Brief facts of the case are that plaintiff (Late Jaswant
Singh) filed a suit for permanent injunction against the
respondents for restraining them from interfering in his
peaceful possession of property. One Swami
Rahuleshwaranand was added as party to the suit as he had
purchased the property in question. On 29.09.2006 plaintiff-Jaswant Singh expired leaving behind his wife-petitioner and
six children. Due to unfortunate demise of Jaswant Singh, the

2
legal heirs moved substitution application Paper No.130-A
on 06.02.2007. The application was moved beyond the period
prescribed for moving substitution application. Thereafter,
application for condonation of delay under section 5 of the
Limitation Act was moved by the legal heirs of the Jaswant
Singh. Against the said application respondent no.3 filed
objection on 12.12.2008. It was submitted that all the legal
heirs neither signed substitution application nor signed the
vakalatnama and the counsel appointed by the legal
representatives had no authority to move substitution
application on behalf of all the legal representatives. On the
objections raised by the defendants-respondents, the court
below vide its order dated 25.03.2009 permitted the
petitioner to remove the defects in the substitution
application Paper No.130-A within one week. Petitioner
moved an amendment application (Paper No.165-A2) on
30.03.2009 stating therein that children of deceased Jaswant
Singh were not available at that time to sign the substitution
application, hence remaining legal heirs i.e. children of
deceased Jaswant Singh may be substituted as performa
defendants. Against the amendment application (Paper
No.165-A2) respondents-defendants filed objection. On
21.04.2009 Additional District Judge/F.T.C.-1 Dehradun
dismissed the amendment application summarily.
 Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the
learned court below overlooked that vide order dated
25.03.2009 the petitioner had been permitted to remove the
defects (errors) in the substitution application within one

3
week and amendment application (Paper No.165-A2) was
filed well within one week. He submitted that the learned
court below overlooked the fact that to remove the defects
(errors) in the pleading, the amendment of the same is the
only remedy available. He also submitted that petitioner is an
illiterate lady and after the death of Jaswant Singh she was
informed about the pendency of the case and at that moment
she could understand the things.

On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent
no.1 & 2 submitted that no plausible explanation has been
given by the petitioner in her application filed under section 5
of the Limitation Act. He also submitted that once property
was sold by Late Jaswant Singh, the actual heirs of Jaswant
Singh have no right over the property in dispute and now
Swami Rahuleshwaranand is the owner of the property. He
also submitted that even after providing sufficient
opportunity for filing substitution application, petitioner did
not file the same in time and instead of that, filed the
amendment application Paper No.165-A2. He submitted that
at the time of filing of substitution application Paper No.130-
A, children (other legal heir) of Jaswant Singh were not
present and they have not signed the substitution application
Paper No.130-A, except the petitioner. He further submitted
that in such circumstances the application of the petitioner
should have been allowed.

I have considered the submissions of learned counsel
for the parties. In my view, seeing the facts and

4
circumstances of the case, the application for amendment
should have been allowed by the Additional District Judge/
F.T.C.-Ist Dehradun. Consequently, the writ petition is
allowed. Order dated 21.04.2009 passed by the Additional
District Judge/F.T.C.-Ist Dehradun is set aside. Application
Paper No.(165-A2) moved by the petitioner for amendment
in substitution application is allowed. Necessary amendment
shall be incorporated by the plaintiff-petitioner in the
substitution application. Thereafter, substitution application
no.130-A shall be considered by the learned court in
accordance with law without being influenced by the
observation made in this order. Considering the fact that the
suit is of the year 1984, I direct the learned trial court to
decide the suit very very expeditiously, preferably within a
period of six months from the date of production of certified
copy of the order.
 Writ petition is disposed of.
